explanation: Use a hash map from keys to stable nodes in a doubly linked recency list. Lookup and insertion of an existing key move its node to the front; an existing key retains its previous price. A new insertion evicts the least-recent node when full, while a nonpositive capacity stores nothing. Every LruCache constructor command clears the previous contents and adopts the supplied new capacity.
timeComplexity: O(1) expected time per lookup, insertion and erase. Initialize discards live entries and clears retained hash storage, taking O(P) worst-case time for the peak entry count P reached during the object's lifetime.
spaceComplexity: O(P) allocated space for peak live entry count P during the object's lifetime. At most the current capacity entries are live, but the hash table can retain previously allocated buckets after erases or resets.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C++ implementation and reset-aware operation wrapper, independently authored from the public problem contract and repository-authored C# algorithm. Uses the unchanged local EPI Judge serialization and test framework APIs; upstream reference sources are not modified.
